transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-11 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM); Tom Lee (Acme CTO), Maya Patel (ML Eng), Carlos Rivera (Infra), Aisha Khan (PM)
Shared links: pilot-benchmarks.csv (drive link), pilot-config.yml, security-deck.pdf

Summary: weekly POC sync to review recent benchmark results, discuss model selection and version pinning strategy, plan canary/rollback windows and next steps.

00:00 Jamie: okay morning everyone thanks for hopping on, quick agenda  - results highlights from Maya's tests, discuss which model variants we want to pin for pilot, and rollout/rollback plan.
00:14 Tom: yeah thanks, trying to keep this short, we got some initial numbers from Maya yesterday but need Redwood's take.
00:27 Priya: cool, I pulled the sheet you shared, maya, and ran a quick pass on latency histograms  - i'll high-level the findings.
00:42 Maya: sorry, had a couple late-night runs, so some of the logs are a bit messy. the main thing: base-13B-fp16 p50 is 240ms but p95 spikes to ~950ms on our 2k token workloads. after quantizing to 8bit we see p50 200ms p95 ~700ms but some quality drop on longer prompts.
01:10 Priya: right, that matches what we see in other customers: quantization yields 15-25% latency improvement and cost reduction, but you need to validate QA/regression on your eval set.
01:28 Jamie: quick Q  - are these runs on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated staging?
01:33 Maya: hosted for now, with the default batching config.
01:38 Priya: ok hosted default batching explains the p95  - we can tune batch cutoffs and KV cache settings to help p95. also note session affinity for chat flows reduces repeated KV compute.
01:55 Carlos: on infra, if we pin a quantized variant for production, we want a rollback to a fp16 variant if we see quality regressions. how does Redwood manage automatic fallback?
02:07 Priya: good question  - we support routing policies: canary rollout based on traffic %, and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if errors or latency SLO breaches occur. we can configure thresholds at p95 latency or error rate.
02:25 Tom: what's the overhead of keeping multiple pinned versions? e.g., memory/GPU pinned.
02:31 Priya: some overhead: dedicated pools with model residency mean GPU memory holds the model. for hosted, model variants are warm/cached  - there is an instance spin-up cost. for dedicated you'd reserve capacity or use burst pools. costs are captured in the sheet.
02:50 Jamie: note for the pilot we recommended pinning one primary serving variant (quantized 8bit) and a fallback (fp16) with canary for 5-10% of traffic for 48 hours. that balances cost and quality.
03:07 Maya: sounds right but we're worried about hallucination increases with 8bit on product recommendations. we need head-to-head evals.
03:16 Priya: absolutely  - propose: Priya will run the head-to-head on your redacted eval set (1k prompts) for three variants: base-13B-fp16, base-13B-8bit, opt-7b-8bit. measure accuracy/QA metrics + latency.
03:33 Aisha: and can you include token cost per 1k tokens and avg tokens per request? finance wants the delta.
03:40 Jamie: we'll include that. the sheet already has cost per 1M tokens for the variants; i'll surface the per-1k line for the pilot.
03:48 Tom: on pinning  - if an update to the model is required (e.g., new weights), how do we handle versioning? can we pin model:v1 and then promote model:v1.1?
03:58 Priya: yes, the catalog supports semantic versioning and immutable model hashes. pinning references model-version IDs, and rollouts can target the new version with a canary percent. rollback is a single button, and we keep previous model in cache for a configured retention window.
04:20 Carlos: retention window  - default?
04:23 Priya: default is 72 hours for warm cache in hosted; on dedicated you can configure residency; on private it's up to you. we can extend retention for the pilot.
04:35 Maya: we saw a couple of timeouts  - roughly 0.8% of requests timed out under burst testing. any quick wins?
04:43 Priya: increase concurrency per worker, tune batching thresholds, and leverage prefix caching for repeated contexts. also consider moving high-frequency flows to a smaller opt-7b variant for cost-sensitive paths.
05:05 Tom: that's interesting  - we have two flow types: short lookup responses (~50 tokens) and long summarization (~1200 tokens). can we route short lookups to opt-7b to save cost and long to base-13b?
05:15 Priya: yes that's a common pattern: routing policies by route or token estimate, with fallbacks. Redwood can do route-based model selection so you can mix models.
05:28 Jamie: any blockers from security/compliance perspective for pinning?
05:31 Carlos: team needs KMS integration validation; we want to ensure model logs are encrypted at rest and there are audit logs for inference.
05:38 Luis: we shared the security-deck last week that shows KMS, SOC2 controls, and audit log capture  - happy to walk through specifics offline.
05:48 Tom: one operational question: during a rollback we lose cache benefits and might see increased latency  - is there a graceful mode?
05:56 Priya: yes, you can configure a phased rollback with canary to gradually shift traffic back, or use a dual-write style where both models serve and you shadow traffic to the new model while the old remains primary until you flip.
06:12 Maya: for our acceptance criteria, we need p95 <= 900ms for long flows and top-1 recommendation accuracy delta <= 1.5% vs baseline. does that seem achievable?
06:24 Priya: p95 target looks feasible with batching and cache tuning. quality delta we'll only know after the eval runs. if quantized variant fails QA we rollback to fp16.
06:34 Jamie: let's capture that as acceptance criteria and action items.
06:40 Tom: another ask  - can Redwood provide a short-lived dedicated pool for load tests to simulate peak?
06:46 Jamie: yes, we can spin a limited dedicated pool for the pilot load tests; pricing differ but we can log it in the sheet and apply pilot credits.
06:54 Aisha: timeline  - we'd like to finalize model choice by 5/18 and begin canary by 5/25.
07:01 Jamie: noted, that's doable.
07:05 Priya: i'll outline the benchmark plan: run 1k prompts across three variants, capture p50/p95, token cost, failure rate, and quality metrics. also run a 30-minute burst test on dedicated staging to measure tail behavior.
07:20 Maya: thanks. one more nuance: our multi-tenant dataset has a subset of sensitive PII, we redacted sample prompts but need to confirm data retention rules  - how long will logs persist?
07:32 Luis: by default 30 days in hosted, but for the pilot we can set retention to 7 days and feed logs to your KMS encrypted archive.
07:40 Carlos: we need SAML/SSO for the console and RBAC for teams.
07:45 Luis: yep, SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported; we'll send the SSO setup doc after.
07:52 Tom: cool.
08:00 Jamie: quick dive into the benchmarks we ran last night  - Priya you want to narrate the sheet?
08:06 Priya: sure. glance at pilot-benchmarks.csv: base-13B-fp16 p50 240ms p95 950ms hosted default batching; base-13B-8bit p50 200ms p95 700ms; opt-7b-8bit p50 120ms p95 450ms. cost-per-1k tokens: base-13B-fp16 $0.9, base-13B-8bit $0.65, opt-7b-8bit $0.35 (pilot pricing).
08:39 Maya: those are approximate but align with what i saw. our quality check: base-13B-fp16 baseline accuracy 92.4%, base-13B-8bit 90.8%, opt-7b-8bit 88.1% on the sample set.
09:00 Tom: hmmm opt-7b looks attractive for short flows but not for recommendations.
09:07 Priya: exactly  - hybrid routing recommended.
09:12 Jamie: what about A/B testing? we should plan to run an A/B for 10% traffic to opt-7b on lookups for 7 days to measure impact.
09:20 Maya: agreed. include instrumentation for drift/quality metrics.
09:25 Priya: we can wire metric hooks to your datadog/tracing and report per-route quality.
09:32 Carlos: any known issues with GPU memory fragmentation with quantized models on dedicated?
09:36 Priya: fragmentation can happen on long-lived hosts; we recommend scheduled model resident maintenance or use of kernel-level allocators we patched to reduce fragmentation. for pilot we can enable aggressive compaction windows during low traffic.
09:53 Tom: rollback SLA  - if we push a model can we guarantee rollback under 15 minutes?
09:58 Luis: rollback by itself is fast for hosted, but cache warmup takes time. we typically plan a 15-60 minute window depending on traffic; we'll instrument and alert on rollback completion.
10:15 Aisha: ok timeline recap?
10:18 Jamie: summarize  - Priya runs 1k prompt benchmark by 5/18; Carlos provisions staging VPC by 5/17; Jamie sends pricing and pilot contract by 5/13; plan canary for 5/25 with 48-hour close monitoring and rollback window.
10:36 Tom: that works. please add the explicit acceptance criteria in the pilot doc: p95 <= 900ms for long flows, top-1 accuracy delta <=1.5% vs baseline, failure rate <=0.5%.
10:50 Priya: will add.
10:55 Maya: note on the sheet i left a comment about sample prompt redaction mismatches, i'll fix and re-upload.
11:00 Jamie: cool. anything else?
11:05 Carlos: one final ask  - can we enable request-level tracing to link model outputs to user sessions for debugging?
11:12 Priya: yes we can include trace ids in the response headers and push to your telemetry; will need SSO service account to configure.
11:22 Tom: thanks everyone. wrap?
11:25 Jamie: thanks all  - we'll follow up with the action items and send updated docs.
11:30 End of call.

Notes on transcription: some product names slightly off in speech (e.g., "key V cache" for KV cache), occasional filler words.

Attachments referenced: pilot-benchmarks.csv (drive://acme/pilot-benchmarks.csv), security-deck.pdf (drive://acme/security/security-deck.pdf), pilot-config.yml (drive://acme/pilot/pilot-config.yml)
